ecological_question: Are species that are normally less recurrent or more seasonally concentrated in the early monitoring period more strongly recruited into the acoustically active assemblage after recent rain in a later time period?
rationale: This tests an episodic-breeder/community-pulse hypothesis using temporally separated baseline traits and validation responses, avoiding construction of the predictor and rainfall response from the same years.

time_split.rule: No baseline trait uses data from 2008-2015; no validation wet/dry response uses data from 2001-2007.

common_run_eligibility.temperature: >=8 valid stop temperatures and mean in [-10,45] C

baseline_traits.species_route_set: For each species, routes on which that species is detected in at least one eligible baseline run.

baseline_recurrence.definition: Among all eligible 2001-2007 runs on the species-specific baseline route set, proportion of runs in which the species is acoustically active.
baseline_recurrence.ecological_meaning: How recurrently the species participates in the active assemblage within places where it was known to occur acoustically during the baseline period.

seasonal_concentration.definition: For RunNumber windows 1-4, calculate effort-standardized activity probability = positive_runs / eligible_runs on the baseline route set. Normalize positive probabilities across windows, calculate Shannon entropy H and effective number exp(H); concentration = 1 - exp(H)/K where K is the number of windows with eligible effort.
seasonal_concentration.range: 0 = activity spread evenly across sampled seasonal windows; values closer to 1 = activity concentrated in fewer windows.

validation_response.pairing: Within each stratum, sort by SurveyYear and pair adjacent observed validation-period years; orient unequal-rain pairs so lower DaysSinceRain is wetter.
validation_response.species_event: For each species present in exactly one member of a pair, y=1 if present only in wetter run, y=0 if present only in drier run.
validation_response.adjusted_species_model: For each eligible species: binomial-logit y ~ centered rain_contrast + centered temp_difference + centered doy_difference + centered year_gap with route-clustered covariance. The centered intercept is the later-period adjusted wet-vs-dry log odds.

primary.model: inverse-variance weighted least squares: validation_adjusted_log_odds ~ baseline_recurrence_logit, HC3 covariance
primary.hypothesis: Species that were less recurrent during 2001-2007 show more positive wet-recruitment responses during 2008-2015.

secondary.model: inverse-variance weighted least squares: validation_adjusted_log_odds ~ baseline_seasonal_concentration, HC3 covariance
secondary.hypothesis: Species whose baseline activity was concentrated into fewer seasonal windows show more positive wet-recruitment responses later.

combined_descriptive.definition: z(-baseline_recurrence_logit) + z(seasonal_concentration), divided by 2; higher = more episodic.
combined_descriptive.status: descriptive only unless both primary and secondary directional hypotheses are supported

family_structure_sensitivity.source: AmphiBIO v1 Family using the previously frozen exact/frozen-genus-alias mapping
tests: within-family permutation of each predictor, 100000 permutations, seed 20260926
family_structure_sensitivity.interpretation: Used to distinguish a species-level ecological gradient from a broad family contrast.

predictions.P1: Primary baseline recurrence slope <0 with 95% CI excluding 0.
predictions.P2: Secondary seasonal concentration slope >0 with 95% CI excluding 0.
predictions.P3: If both P1 and P2 hold, rainfall preferentially recruits historically episodic species into the active assemblage.
predictions.P4: If only P1 holds, interpretation is low-recurrence recruitment rather than seasonal specialization.
predictions.P5: If neither holds, species-selective reassembly remains real but is not explained by baseline episodicity.

boundaries: Baseline recurrence is acoustic participation recurrence, not occupancy probability.
Seasonal concentration reflects NAAMP sampling windows, not a complete annual breeding phenology curve.
The same species are observed across time; this is temporal holdout validation, not an independent-species replication.
No rainfall causality, breeding success, colonization, or extinction claim.
No thresholds or additional baseline traits may be added after readback within this analysis family.
